about.title: Mission Viejo Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription:
Three people died on Mission Viejo roads in 2025, according to the most recent final crash records. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Orange County that has to keep going without someone at the table. If that is your family right now, you do not need to understand the legal process today. You only need to know that help exists and that it does not have to cost anything up front.

A wrongful death claim in California is a civil case, separate from anything the police or a prosecutor may be doing. It asks whether someone's negligence — on I-5, along Marguerite Parkway or Alicia Parkway, at a workplace, in a care setting — caused the loss, and what that loss means for the people left behind. Funeral and burial costs, the income your loved one would have provided, and the companionship and guidance that cannot be replaced are all part of that conversation.

We handle wrongful death claims on contingency, meaning you pay nothing unless we recover for your family.

whyChoose.title: What a Mission Viejo Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Not everyone can file, and the order matters
items.desc: California gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs following. We can sort out who in your family has standing so the claim is filed correctly the first time.

items.title: The clock runs from the date of death
items.desc: You generally have two years from the day your loved one died to file, and the window is shorter when a city, county, or state agency may be responsible. Reaching out early protects your family's options.

items.title: The law recognizes more than the bills
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses and the financial support your loved one would have provided, but also the love, companionship, and guidance that has been taken from you. We work to account for all of it, on contingency.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on I-5 near Mission Viejo. Where do we start?
items.answer: Start by taking care of yourselves; the legal steps can wait a few days. When you are ready, gather whatever you have — the CHP or police report number, insurance information, and any medical or funeral paperwork. Contact us, and we will review what happened on the San Diego Freeway and explain whether a wrongful death claim makes sense for your family.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, separate from any criminal prosecution in Orange County. The two cases can proceed at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. We can also help make sure the two-year civil deadline is not missed while the criminal case unfolds.

items.question: We were not married, but we lived together for years. Can I bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California puts a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and children first in line, and then allows certain people who were financially dependent on the deceased to file. Whether you qualify depends on your specific relationship and circumstances, which is exactly the kind of question we can answer during a free consultation.
